mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid government-issued photo identification (e.g., passport) of each director, officer, promoter and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / Commissioner of Oaths in the country of issue
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the competent authority in the country of issue; where the country is not a party to the Apostille Convention, consular legalization by a Canadian embassy/consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Corporate Existence for any shareholder that is a corporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, Hong Kong Companies Registry, Delaware Division of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing jurisdiction is a Hague Contracting State; otherwise consular legalization by a Canadian diplomatic post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / source-of-funds confirmation for the initial capital subscription
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized by the issuing bank's authorized officer; apostille or consular legalization required when the bank or the signature is outside Canada and not covered by an exception

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Canadian incorporation agent, where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The proposed directors/shareholders acting as principals
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execution under oath before a Canadian notary or commissioner, or apostille/consular legalization of the principal's foreign signature

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation, every director, officer, promoter and holder of 25% or more of significant control must be screened against the consolidated UN Security Council list, the Canadian consolidated sanctions list under the United Nations Act and the Special Economic Measures Act, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act list, and the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list where U.S.-dollar payment rails are relevant. Domestic and foreign politically exposed persons and heads of international organizations must be identified and subjected to enhanced due diligence. A negative match must be documented in the corporate KYC file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre and NUANS Name Search (https://www.ic.gc.ca/app/scr/cc/CorporationsCanada/registries?returnUrl=)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A federal corporation may choose a name in English, French, or both official languages, except where the CBCA regulations require the bilingual form. The name must include a distinct legal element such as Limited, Limitée, Corporation, Incorporée, Corp., Inc., Ltée, or the full equivalents. If a name is derived from a non-official script, a transliteration into English or French must be supplied. The name must be distinctive and must not be confusingly similar with any corporate, trademark, or registered trade-name protected in Canada. The Director may require a French version of the name, particularly where the corporation carries on business in Quebec or in bilingual federal settings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Director refuses a proposed name under CBCA s. 12, the applicant may apply to the Federal Court or the competent superior court for judicial review within 21 days of receiving the refusal notice. Before such application, an informal reconsideration is recommended, supported by a fresh NUANS report, evidence of prior use or trademark registration, and a legal memorandum addressing distinctiveness and confusion. Names rejected because they contain a sensitive token cannot be cured by appeal to the Director; approval must first be obtained from the responsible federal or provincial regulator. The 90-day validity of a NUANS report cannot be extended; a new search and fee are required for a fresh filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only if it provides a physical street address in the designated province, is not a post office box, and has an operator who accepts service of process on behalf of the corporation. Purely mail-forwarding or non-serviceable addresses are not compliant with the CBCA. For the designer blind box e-commerce industry, banks and merchant processors such as Shopify Payments, Stripe, and local POS acquirers will generally require a real operating address or a registered commercial address with administrative substance; a bare virtual office may trigger additional AML screening and underwriting review.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 5% annualised risk for a low-risk e-commerce designer-toy distributor of this profile. Corporations Canada does not routinely conduct unannounced inspections of CBCA registered offices; however, Canada Revenue Agency or provincial consumer protection authorities may verify the registered office as part of an audit or upon receipt of a complaint. The risk rises if the beneficial ownership structure involves high-risk foreign jurisdictions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44 (CBCA), including sections 5 (incorporation eligibility), 6 (articles of incorporation), 10 (registered office), 11 (corporate name), 12 (articles filing), 19 (corporate records), 102 (board of directors), 105 (director qualifications), 115 (board meetings), 117 (notice of directors), 118 (share issuance), 119 (director residency), 120 (disclosure of interests), 121 (officers), 125 (corporate capacity), and 146 (unanimous shareholder agreement).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act, filed using Corporations Canada Form 1 or the Corporations Canada online incorporation service, together with the registered office and first board information required by the Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The CBCA imposes no minimum authorized capital, issued capital, or paid-up capital requirement and does not require a statutory escrow account. Shares may be issued for consideration consisting of money, property, or past services, provided the consideration is not less than the fair equivalent of the consideration received. The corporation should maintain subscription records, issue share certificates or electronic ownership records, and record consideration received in its securities register. The stated USD amount is an approximate conversion of the official CAD 200 online incorporation fee; the registry charges in Canadian dollars and the USD equivalent fluctuates.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the corporation adopt its registered office at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation and authorize the officers to update the registered office filing when required. RESOLVED THAT the subscription for the issued shares described in the incorporation documents is approved and the shares are issued to the subscribers upon receipt of the agreed consideration, which shall be recorded in the securities register. RESOLVED THAT [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board. RESOLVED THAT the officers are authorized to open bank and payment accounts and execute all incorporation and operational documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Select Corporate Name and Confirm Federal Availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online name search and incorporation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a word name or numbered company. For a word name, conduct a Nuans corporate name search and obtain the required Nuans report. Ensure the name is distinctive, not confusing with an existing business, and does not imply government sponsorship or an unauthorized professional activity. A numbered corporation may generally be incorporated without a Nuans report.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-company request
Nuans name search report, if a word name is selected
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, submit an amended name, a fresh Nuans report where required, or incorporate as a numbered company and seek a subsequent corporate name amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and File Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online incorporation service or Corporations Canada filing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 or the online equivalent, specifying the corporate name, registered office province, share structure, transfer restrictions, number of directors, director residency provisions, and any incorporation restrictions. Identify the incorporator and initial directors. Submit the articles, required registered-office and director information, and the CAD 200 online fee. Non-Canadian shareholders may own shares, subject to applicable director-residency rules and any sector-specific restrictions.
required_dossiers: Initial director information and written consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct clerical or substantive deficiencies through the Corporations Canada online correspondence process. If the filing is refused, resubmit corrected articles or request reconsideration from Corporations Canada. Preserve the filing reference and all registry communications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate and Establish Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada and the corporation's registered records office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the certificate of incorporation, filed articles, and corporate information. Create the minute book and maintain the registered office, central securities register, register of directors and officers, register of individuals with significant control, share subscription records, director consents, and organizational resolutions. Prepare the individuals-with-significant-control register and keep it at the registered office or another permitted Canadian location.
required_dossiers: Register of individuals with significant control
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify omissions through directors' resolutions, corrected registers, and applicable articles or information filings. Material historical inaccuracies should be documented and corrected promptly, with legal advice where the error affects share ownership or corporate authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Organizational Resolutions and Issue Shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors and registered records office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first directors' meeting or execute a written directors' resolution. Adopt the registered office, appoint officers, approve banking arrangements, authorize tax and payment accounts, approve the business plan, and issue shares for documented consideration. Record the issuance in the securities register and deliver certificates or electronic ownership evidence. Confirm director and officer conflict-of-interest procedures under the CBCA.
required_dossiers: Share certificates or electronic ownership records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Pass confirming or ratifying resolutions, correct the securities register, and obtain replacement certificates where necessary. Unclear or defective issuances should be reviewed before further transfers, financing, or dividend declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Provincial, Municipal, and Employer Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online, applicable provincial or territorial corporate registry, municipality, and provincial workplace authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a CRA business number and register for GST/HST when required or voluntarily. Register extra-provincially in each province or territory where the corporation carries on business. Obtain municipal business licences, zoning confirmation, occupancy approval, building permits, and fire approvals for the manufacturing or warehouse premises. Register payroll, workers' compensation, and employer health or safety accounts where applicable.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and corporate profile
Payroll and workers' compensation registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to registry or municipal information requests, provide corrected lease, zoning, ownership, or director documents, and appeal or seek reconsideration under the applicable provincial or municipal procedure if a licence is refused.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No single federal industrial licensing board applies to ordinary designer-toy manufacturing. The competent authorities are the province or territory, municipality, local building and fire authority, and applicable environmental regulator. Federal product-safety oversight is administered by Health Canada's Consumer Product Safety Directorate.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general federal manufacturing licence for rotocasting, injection, airbrush finishing, or designer-toy merchandising. Applicable permits may include a municipal business licence, zoning or occupancy approval, building permit, fire approval, provincial environmental permit, wastewater authorization, air-emissions approval, and hazardous-waste registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally exempt from a federal impact assessment for a standalone small or medium-sized toy manufacturing facility because ordinary toy manufacturing is not generally a designated project under the Physical Activities Regulations. A provincial or territorial screening, permit, registration, or environmental assessment may nevertheless apply based on facility size, emissions, wastewater, land disturbance, or location.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with applicable provincial, territorial, and municipal limits for wastewater discharge, stormwater, air contaminants, particulate matter, VOCs, odours, and hazardous materials. Use appropriate ventilation and controls for paints, solvents, adhesives, and plastic-processing emissions. Store and dispose of paint residues, solvents, contaminated filters, scrap materials, and other regulated waste through authorized handlers. Federal product-safety requirements include the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act and Toys Regulations, SOR/2011-17, including prohibitions on unsafe products and applicable requirements concerning small parts, toxic substances, flammability, surface coatings, and records. Exact numeric thresholds depend on the province, municipality, facility equipment, substances, and receiving sewer or water body.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal building permits, occupancy approval, fire inspection or fire-safety certification, and approvals for emergency exits, fire detection, suppression systems, storage, and hazardous materials where required. Obtain structural-load and equipment-installation approvals for production lines, mezzanines, racking, compressed-air systems, and material-handling equipment where applicable. Comply with the occupational health and safety legislation of the province or territory, including machine guarding, ventilation, chemical management, safety data sheets, personal protective equipment, workplace training, incident reporting, and workers' compensation registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) – My Business Account portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign corporation carrying on business in Canada must obtain a Business Number (BN) from the CRA. Registration can be completed online through Business Registration Online (BRO), by mailing Form RC1, or by using the CRA's My Business Account interface after basic identity validation. The BN is the single statutory identifier; separate CRA program accounts are opened for GST/HST (RT account), payroll (RP account), and corporate income tax (RC account) as required. Non-resident corporations are eligible to register if they have a Canadian establishment, carry on business in Canada, or make taxable supplies in Canada; a representative may be required for non-resident registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists in Canada. A federal or provincial business corporation is mandatorily taxed as a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act. Relevant statutory elections include the s. 216(1) election for a non-resident to compute Canadian rental income on a net basis, the s. 219(2) election to be deemed a resident Canadian corporation for certain Part I purposes, and various joint elections for related corporations and loss-transfers under ss. 256(7) and 256(8). Hybrid mismatch rules in ss. 18.4-18.8 ITA deny inappropriate deduction/non-inclusion outcomes and do not create elective classification flexibility.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide gross revenue from taxable supplies other than zero-rated supplies, assessed over the prior four consecutive calendar quarters or any single quarter; once exceeded, mandatory GST/HST registration is required. Non-resident vendors making taxable supplies in Canada through any physical or digital presence are subject to the same threshold, with a simplified non-resident GST/HST registration procedure available.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping mandate exists at the federal level. CRA accepts electronic invoices and sales records provided they are complete, legible, and retained for six years. GST/HST returns and prescribed information must be filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE, CRA My Business Account, or approved EDI/API channels where applicable; there is no requirement for government pre-approval of each invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods exported by the supplier as part of a commercial activity, provided the goods are physically shipped from Canada to a destination outside Canada and title passes to a non-resident recipient. Under Part V, Section 1 of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, the supply of goods is zero-rated if the supplier has proof of export within the prescribed time. Services supplied to non-residents may be zero-rated if performed wholly outside Canada or if they qualify as listed services such as advisory, consulting, research, software, or telecommunication services. For designer blind-box toys, zero-rating is available where the goods are sold remotely to foreign customers, shipped by commercial carrier, and export documentation is retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13A or electronic equivalent) where an export reporting requirement applies
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / carrier waybill showing shipment from Canada to foreign destination
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying goods, quantities, values, and foreign consignee
Written payment evidence, including SWIFT transfer, inward remittance certificate, or credit-card settlement record from the e-commerce payment processor
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA routinely audits export zero-rating claims and may deny zero-rating where export evidence is incomplete, unreliable, or not contemporaneous. If denied, the supplier is assessed tax on the full selling price with interest from the reporting date. Penalties include false-statement penalties under s. 280(1) of the Excise Tax Act equal to 25% of the net tax alleged to be payable, and the gross-negligence penalty under s. 285(1) equal to 50% of the understated net tax. Deliberate fraud may trigger criminal prosecution under s. 327 ETA with fines up to CAD 25,000 and imprisonment of up to two years. Any GST/HST input tax credits or refunds claimed in respect of the export transaction are clawed back in full.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Canada's central bank), external exchange administration delegated to the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for deposit-taking institution supervision and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for cross-border wire reporting and anti-money-laundering compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains no foreign exchange control legislation and no requirement for central bank approval on current-account trade settlements, capital injections, or profit repatriation. The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts under the Currency Act and Bank Act. Profit remittance via dividends is permissible but is subject to corporate law solvency tests under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) and, for non-resident shareholders, to Canadian withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, with treaty reduction available under the applicable bilateral tax treaty. In practice, cross-border treasury flows are cleared freely through the Canadian bank-owned LYNX high-value payment system or via correspondent banks using SWIFT MT103 messages.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory export proceeds surrender ratio, and no foreign currency conversion obligation. Exporters may retain invoice settlement proceeds in foreign currencies and convert them at negotiated Schedule I bank rates. Although no central bank reporting is required for export revenues, all cross-border electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or above must be reported to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and the underlying commercial documents must be preserved for compliance audits.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for cross-border payout disbursement and FX conversion sub-liquidity, but Low as a primary treasury or capital escrow rail. Offshore electronic money institutions holding no Canadian banking licence are not authorised by OSFI to take deposits from Canadian residents in Canada and do not benefit from the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) protection. If a foreign EMI onboards the Canadian corporation, it must be registered in Canada as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC where applicable, and the arrangement should be limited to a fintech distribution wallet rather than central treasury clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a low-risk standard designer-toy exporter, remote account opening is technically feasible at tier-one banks through use of digital identity verification, notarised corporate certificates, and video interview for authorised signatories. However, most Schedule I Canadian banks in practice require an in-branch presence at a business banking centre or a private banking/International Banking Centre interview for corporate account onboarding, especially where a director or ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident. Non-resident directors may satisfy KYC through a notarised apostilled passport copy, a certified copy of the CBCA Certificate of Incorporation, and a physically signed corporate onboarding package delivered via courier; a remote video interview by bank compliance is increasingly accepted but should not be assumed for top-five bank onboarding without relationship-manager pre-approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or ultimate beneficial owner residing in a non-sanctioned but tax-transparent jurisdiction, creating beneficial ownership opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Federal Certificate of Incorporation, CBCA Articles of Amendment, complete Register of Directors, up-to-date central securities register satisfying CBCA beneficial ownership transparency rules, notarised and apostilled passports for all 25%-plus owners, CRS self-certification forms, corporate structural diagram, and signed director resolution designating the Canadian treasury signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Start-up cash flows showing high-frequency aggregated settlements from Shopify Payments, Stripe, and local point-of-sale channels with no matching underlying commercial documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sales order lifecycle documents, commercial invoices, packing lists, carrier pickup confirmation, shipping manifest, Canadian GST/HST account returns, aggregated merchant settlement statements, refund policy documentation, and e-commerce platform data export proving physical toy delivery rather than money-service or gambling activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contribution from a foreign parent labelled as a private 'gift' or 'loan' without corporate authority, triggering source-of-funds review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed equity subscription agreement, CBCA board resolution authorising share issuance, share certificate register entries, audited or reviewed parent-company financial statements, bank account proof in the parent's name, explanation of the USD/CAD capital contribution economics, and a currency conversion forecast demonstrating legitimate treasury need.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound trade settlements directed to toy manufacturing counterparties in higher-risk Asian jurisdictions with third-party payment routing, mismatched invoice names, or dual-use machinery references.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Factory AML due diligence file, manufacturing contract between the Canadian entity and the supplier, commercial invoice and packing list, full-set transport documents, customs entry records, bank SWIFT MT103 reimbursement evidence, supplier business registration certificate, and signed supplier attestation of lawful manufacturing exclusivity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign parent subscription proceeds are sent by SWIFT MT103 to the Canadian corporation's Schedule I bank account, using SWIFT BIC plus Canadian institution/transit and account number. The remittance field must state 'Equity capital contribution under Canada Business Corporations Act resolution dated YYYY-MM-DD; subscription for [X] common shares at CAD [value] per share'; no Canadian foreign-exchange-control approval is required. The receiving bank conducts sanctions and PEP screening; the corporation must verify beneficial owner consistency, retain the executed subscription agreement, board resolution, and bank credit advice notice in the compliance file, and ensure the transaction is booked as common-share capital surplus on the balance sheet.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 or commercial letters of credit issued by the Canadian relationship bank and advised through correspondent banking to Asian suppliers. For urgent pre-shipment deposits to vinyl toy manufacturing contractors, MT103 priority 'S' with remittance reference to the commercial invoice is the standard clearing rail. CAD-denominated high-value settlements use LYNX, the Canadian high-value payment system; US-dollar settlements clear over Fedwire or CHIPS through the bank's US correspondent; cross-border euro or renminbi settlements rely on correspondent bank SWIFT routing. For documentary trade, an irrevocable at-sight commercial LC with a confirmed negotiating bank mitigates supplier payment risk while preserving clean export documentation for Canadian customs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable FX forward contracts (tenors typically up to 12 months) executed under an ISDA or Canadian Bankers' Association master agreement with a regulated Schedule I/III Canadian bank, limited to hedging underlying export sales and royalty cash flows;

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic non-CAD pair exposures where local currency delivery is legally prohibited, are acceptable only as a treasury overlay through a highly rated global bank and should not be used for CAD because CAD is fully deliverable in the Canadian onshore market;

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (currency swaps) between CAD and USD to swap fixed-rate capital injection liabilities into floating USD trade-payable flows, permitted for non-speculative treasury risk management under Bank Act prudential rules and OSFI margin requirements.

stage_5.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (records and annual return certification)
stage_5.receiving_authority: No external regulatory filing; minutes retained at registered office; AGM notice must be delivered within 21 to 60 days
stage_5.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation; thereafter one per calendar year and no later than 15 months after prior AGM
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: Directors/ officers who fail to call the AGM may be liable to fines up to CAD 5,000; failure to certify in the annual return exposes the corporation to administrative dissolution if un-remedied

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate income tax rate (Income Tax Act s. 123(1.1)); combined federal–provincial headline rate approximately 26.5%–31% depending on province of establishment
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 9% SBD federal rate on first CAD 500,000 active business income for CCPCs (s. 125); 46.25% taxable-capital-gains inclusion? No — better:
